subject: Segregated fleet scenarios: capacity & commercial tradeoffs for regulated workloads
messages:
From: Emma Torres <emma.torres@apexcare.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: initial inquiry - isolated fleet for PHI workloads

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the helpful call earlier. We are evaluating options for hosting an inference stack that will process PHI. Two initial constraints: (1) data residency requirements (US only), and (2) strict audit / log retention for 3 years.

We're trying to decide whether Redwood Dedicated (reserved, isolated GPU pools in your cloud) or a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem package) makes more sense operationally and commercially. Key questions on our side:
- Minimum GPU footprint to meet 99th percentile latency of 150ms for short-chat flows (~40 tokens) at 10 qps.
- Cost delta between an annual dedicated commitment vs a one-time private licensing + infra estimate.
- Procurement timeline / any SOC2 evidence you can share upfront.

Can you point us to an apples-to-apples sizing sketch and a procurement checklist? We can share sample traffic patterns if that helps.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Torres
Head of Cloud & Platforms, ApexCare
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emma Torres <emma.torres@apexcare.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-22T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Segregated fleet scenarios: capacity & commercial tradeoffs for regulated workloads

Hi Emma — great to hear the constraints. If you can share the traffic sample that will help, but I sketched two high-level scenarios based on the 10 qps target:

1) Dedicated (Reserved GPU pool, isolated tenancy in our cloud)
- Baseline: 4 x A100-80GB-equivalent workers in a dedicated pool, autoscale to 8 for 99th percentile headroom.
- Latency target: ~120-160ms p99 for 40-token requests depending on model and batching.
- Benefits: fast time-to-value, Redwood manages HW/patching, standard SLAs.
- Commercial: annual commit with monthly billing; ramp discounts available.

2) Private (VPC-hosted or on-prem)
- Baseline: 6 x A100-80GB-equivalent to maintain lower cold-cache p99 and allow for isolated backups.
- Latency target: slightly better consistency (110-150ms p99) but depends on your infra ops.
- Benefits: full data isolation, KMS/HSM integration, customer controls retention/audit logs.
- Commercial: platform license + deployment services; CapEx + one-time onboarding; optional annual support fee.

I'll pull together a short workbook with assumptions and a cost delta. Looping in Marissa (enterprise sales) for procurement path and Lauren for compliance evidence.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-25T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Segregated fleet scenarios: capacity & commercial tradeoffs for regulated workloads

Emma / team — attached is a compact model (capacity_model_apexcare_v1.xlsx) with three traffic profiles you mentioned (baseline/peak/black-swan). High-level callouts:

- For your steady 10 qps baseline we model requests at 40 tokens avg and assume model = open-mix-7b-quant (conservative).
- Dedicated: 4 reserved workers covers baseline with autoscale headroom; cost per month (incl. reserved compute + software) is estimated at $32k/month. Annual commitment reduces to ~ $27k/month effective.
- Private (VPC-managed by you): software license + deployment services estimated at a $240k one-time onboarding + $6k/month support. You will have to provision and operate the hardware (we included a notional CapEx estimate of $160k for 4 A100-class GPUs + network + NTP/HSM integration).

Operational trade: Dedicated reduces your operational burden and gives Redwood responsibility for patching, kernel updates, and predictable autoscaling. Private gives you the tightest control over logs and audit integrations. In many regulated customers we recommend Dedicated when the customer accepts that the control plane is hosted but data plane is isolated to a dedicated tenant and network controls.

Attachments: SOW_apexcare_draft.pdf (SOW draft), deployment_option_onepager.pdf (one-pager summaries).

Next steps we recommend: 1) Review model assumptions in the workbook and flag any differences in token distribution or peak qps, 2) Marissa to send a formal pricing slide + procurement checklist, 3) Lauren to provide SOC2 / audit artifact list.

Thanks — I can also run a 48-hour load test on a trial dedicated pool to validate p99 if you want.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Recommendation (short): Start with a 6-month Dedicated reserved pool (4 workers baseline, auto-scale to 8) with the option to convert to Private within the first 12 months if you require deeper host-level controls. Rationale: minimizes time-to-value, keeps operating cost predictable during product-market fit, and still satisfies data residency and audit requirements via dedicated tenancy and KMS integrations.

Commercial ask: If ApexCare is willing to commit to a 12-month reserved term we can offer a 15% discount off the listed dedicated pricing and include an onboarding credit to run the 48-hour production-equivalent load test.

Procurement items attached/linked: SOW_apexcare_draft.pdf, capacity_model_apexcare_v1.xlsx, deployment_option_onepager.pdf, HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/2781
